newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels kill nine in latest clashes.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels kill nine in latest clashes.

text.p: Leftist rebels stepped up their nationwide offensive, killing nine people, including civilians and security force members, in four separate attacks, Colombian authorities said on Friday.

A 250-strong column of National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas killed five policemen, two women and a child in a five-hour firefight on Thursday night in the eastern town of Cubara near the border with Venezuela, a police spokesman said.
Three people were injured and the Cubara police post was completely destroyed, the spokesman added.

"Five men died in the attack. There were initial reports that 10 police had disappeared but they withdrew and continued fighting on other fronts," said deputy national police chief Gen. Luis Ernesto Gilibert.
Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) insurgents killed a soldier in an assault on an army base in Usme, just 15 miles (25 km) south of the capital.
Two policemen and three marines were injured in two other attacks by the FARC on Thursday night.
The latest fighting came soon after four days of savage combat in the mountain community of San Juanito just 30 miles (50 km) east of Bogota, in which 16 soldiers died.

Political analysts believe the FARC, Colombia's largest rebel army set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964, and the ELN, set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in the mid-1960s, will escalate their attacks this year.
